payload.summary: Bounded discovery complete. src/greeting.mjs is a 3-line module exporting only greet(name) => `Hello, ${name}!`; that template literal is the sole extraction target. src/format.mjs does not exist yet. Two configured required validators (.harness/project.yaml validation.commands fixture-greeting -> node scripts/validate.mjs; validation.validators contract-test -> node scripts/contract.mjs) assert greet is a function, greet("AEH")==="Hello, AEH!", and that greeting.mjs's dynamic-import export keys are within ["greet","FAREWELL"]. A third real gate, scripts/architecture.mjs (npm run check:architecture), already anticipates the refactor: it requires greeting.mjs to export exactly ["greet"], requires an import specifier exactly './format.mjs' once src/format.mjs exists, and forbids format.mjs importing greeting.mjs. No specs/tests/contracts directories exist; the three scripts are the test surface. No files edited.

risks: Export-style trap: architecture.mjs counts only `export (const|function|class)` tokens in greeting.mjs; moving greet to format.mjs and re-exporting it (`export { greet } from './format.mjs'`) would yield an empty export list and fail `greeting public export surface`. greet must remain a declared export in greeting.mjs (e.g. import { formatGreeting } from './format.mjs'; export function greet(name){ return formatGreeting(name); }).
Specifier trap: architecture.mjs requires the literal import form `from "./format.mjs"` (or single quotes) in greeting.mjs; alternate specifiers or extensionless imports fail.
Cycle trap: format.mjs importing greeting.mjs in any form fails architecture.mjs line 14.
Behavior trap: contract/validate compare against the exact string 'Hello, AEH!' - any change to spacing/punctuation/punctuation of the template breaks both required validators.
Scope trap: adding any extra export to greeting.mjs (even FAREWELL, which contract.mjs tolerates) fails architecture.mjs's exact-equality check against ['greet'].
